sources.title: Kokou Azamede, Die Funkstation von Kamina (2014), Goethe-Institut Togo
sources.note: Togolese scholar’s institutional historical-site account, directly read in full. Construction, support works, approximately 100 coerced workers, radio link and destruction. Do not use its 27 August surrender date, which differs from standard military chronology; public copy uses month only.

sources.title: Kokou Azamede, Eine Uniform für den Togo: Schule in Togo, Goethe University collections
sources.note: Direct full scholarly collection essay read. Photograph StuUB Bildnr. 035-3510-20 by Reinhold Schober is probably 1933 to 1937, not German-colonial era. Essay distinguishes school history from later visual evidence. Avoid inferring pupils’ feelings or bystander envy from photograph.

sources.title: British Museum, Ewe cloth made into a gown, Af1966,01.12
sources.note: Full indexed primary collection catalogue checked. Cotton cloth circa 1900 to 1920, eastern Ghana or Togo; supplementary weft. Curator interprets gown as later tailoring of rectangular Ewe formal cloth. Direct fetch failed.

sources.title: British Museum, fibre and leather apron, Af1919,1220.5
sources.note: Full indexed primary catalogue checked. Registered Frafra, museum maps label to Grusi; colonial Togo broad provenance includes present Ghana. 1914 to 1919 inferred collection interval, not secure manufacturing date; exact village and acquisition circumstances unknown.

sources.title: Diedrich Westermann, Wörterbuch der Ewe-Sprache, volume 1 (1905), p. 356
sources.note: Primary dictionary OCR downloaded from public Archive, local westermann-1905-ocr.txt, lines 53174 to 53178 under amla on printed p. 356. Exact Akpafumla and German definition: type of bush knife also used as hoe, made chiefly in Akpafu. Spelling corroborated independently by Dingemanse 2011 thesis note 72, https://pure.mpg.de/pubman/item/item_1005623_17/component/file_3341064/dingemanse-2011-thesis.pdf, indexed; direct PDF 403. No original page image claimed.

sources.title: United Nations Trusteeship Council, historical account of the Togoland unification question
sources.note: UN report indexed text checked, section II paragraphs 9 to 12. Direct PDF 403. Records 1919 boundary declaration and quotes September 1919 chiefs’ petition on Ewe separation and economic concerns. Use as documentary record of petitioners’ expressed concerns.

proposedOverrides.name: Togoland
proposedOverrides.summary: German Togoland’s wartime conquest and partition, followed by British and French colonial administration.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Distinct colonial transition record, not modern Togo. Point-in-polygon checks confirm Lomé, Kamina and Akpafu within imported geometry. Historical colony included present Ghana and Togo, museum objects with broad colonial provenance cannot be assigned automatically to today’s Togo. No shared card with modern Togo. Map endpoint precedes formal 1922 mandates; later school photo explicitly 1933 to 1937.
